newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Israel to suffer for settlement policy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Israel to suffer for settlement policy.

text.p: Egypt's representative at the Arab League warned Israel on Wednesday that it was facing isolation in the region if it did not reconsider its settlement policy in the disputed city of Jerusalem.
The Jewish state has angered its Arab neighbours and Palestinian peace partners by building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Arabs say the project has put the Middle East peace process in jeopardy and prompted the Gulf state of Oman to freeze all ties with Israel at a weekend Organisation of Islamic Conference meeting.
"Israel will pay dearly if it does not stop its settlement policy... the government has to realise that Oman's action will not be a solitary one," Ambassador Wagih Hamdi told reporters.
"Israel has gained a lot from having peaceful ties... jeopardising the peace process amounts to jeopardising its own interests," he added.

Egypt became the first Arab country to make peace with Israel when they signed a peace treaty in 1979. Jordan also has peaceful ties with its Jewish neighbour while the rest of the Arab world officially ignores it.
Hamdi said the Jerusalem settlement on Jebel Abu Ghneim or Har Homa would dominate a foreign ministers meeting of the 22-member league which will be held in Cairo on March 30.
The Jerusalem Committee will also meet in Morocco on Thursday to discuss ways to counter Israeli policies.
